note: Anti-VEGF reached DME from AMD: the DME-like models (STZ-rat Evans-blue leak, VEGF-injected monkey) were never set against RISE/RIDE or VIVID/VISTA, EMA accepted the aflibercept and faricimab DME filings with no DME-specific nonclinical model, and the only stated model-patient comparison is brolucizumab's in-vitro immunogenicity screen, which the FDA reviewer said correctly predicted intraocular inflammation (in nAMD patients, later reproduced in DME).
label: DME (anti-VEGF)

engagement.model: STZ-diabetic rat, Evans-blue retinal leak, systemic VEGF Trap
engagement.note: Systemic VEGF TrapA40 abolished diabetes-induced retinal leak in 1-week STZ rats; no paper set this against DME-patient VEGF suppression.
engagement.short: VEGF Trap abolished leak in diabetic rats
engagement.quote: Diabetes-induced blood-retinal barrier breakdown was dose-dependently inhibited with VEGF TrapA(40), with 25 mg/kg producing complete inhibition of the diabetes-induced increases (P < 0.05).
engagement.judgement: Patient-side engagement exists in DME (Muether 2014, doi:10.1136/bjophthalmol-2013-303954: aqueous VEGF completely suppressed for a mean 33.7 days after ranibizumab in 17 DME eyes) but it cites no model; setting the two side by side would be our juxtaposition, so untested. IOVS 2001 carries no DOI (PubMed esummary confirms), hence the PubMed URL. Abstract-level reading. VEGF TrapA40 is a Regeneron precursor construct, not aflibercept.

dose.model: Rabbit-half-life mathematical model of intravitreal VEGF-binding activity
dose.note: First-order decay model from rabbit half-lives predicted 10-12 weeks of VEGF Trap activity; VIVID/VISTA 2q8 ≈ 2q4 was never compared with it.
dose.quote: On the basis of this mathematical model, VEGF Trap maintains significant intravitreal VEGF-binding activity for 10-12 weeks after a single injection.
dose.judgement: DME dosing was carried over from AMD (VIEW). Korobelnik 2014 (doi:10.1016/j.ophtha.2014.05.006) reports 'similar efficacy in the 2q4 and 2q8 groups despite the extended dosing interval in the 2q8 group' but cites no model. Luu 2020 (doi:10.1124/jpet.119.263178) translated a rabbit PK/PD model of abicipar and 'refitted' it to DME and nAMD patient aqueous-humour and serum concentrations: a refit, not a tested prediction; full text paywalled (HTTP 403), abstract only. Registry: VIVID NCT01331681 results first posted 2014-09-09; VISTA NCT01363440 2015-04-20. Ranibizumab's 0.3 mg DME dose (RISE/RIDE, NCT00473330/NCT00473382, results posted 2013-01-17) came from clinical dose arms, not a model.

efficacy.model: STZ-diabetic rat, Evans-blue retinal leak (plus VEGF-injected monkey)
efficacy.note: STZ-rat Evans-blue leak model; EMA found no DME-specific nonclinical data filed for aflibercept (2014) or faricimab (2022); no model-trial comparison published.
efficacy.short: No DME model filed or compared
efficacy.quote: VEGF inhibition should prove a useful therapeutic approach in the treatment of early diabetic blood-retinal barrier breakdown.
efficacy.reason: Regulators saw no DME model; none compared
efficacy.judgement: EMA Eylea DME extension (EMEA/H/C/002392/II/0009, CHMP opinion 26 June 2014; https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/variation-report/eylea-h-c-2392-ii-0009-epar-assessment-report-variation_en.pdf): 'No new non-clinical data have been submitted in this application, which was considered acceptable by the CHMP.' Vabysmo EPAR (EMA/687844/2022; https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/assessment-report/vabysmo-epar-public-assessment-report_en.pdf): 'The CHMP noted that the Applicant presented the in vivo experimental model only for nAMD and not for DME, in contrast with the intended indications of faricimab' and 'classical animal models of diabetes could not work' because faricimab does not bind rodent VEGF-A (the CHMP suggested spontaneously diabetic cynomolgus monkeys; 'not a blocking issue'). Tolentino 1996 (doi:10.1016/s0161-6420(96)30420-x) showed intravitreal VEGF alone produces DR-like leak, oedema and microaneurysms in cynomolgus monkeys: target validation, no drug tested. No primary source compares any permeability model with RISE/RIDE (Nguyen 2012, doi:10.1016/j.ophtha.2011.12.039; results posted 2013-01-17) or VIVID/VISTA (Korobelnik 2014) or YOSEMITE/RHINE (Wykoff 2022, doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(22)00018-6; NCT03622580/NCT03622593 results posted 2022-03-22). Drugs@FDA posts only approval letters and labels for the Lucentis (2012) and Eylea (2014) DME supplements and for faricimab BLA 761235, so no FDA pharmacology review names a DME model (model_filed false).

safety.model: In-vitro human PBMC T-cell immunogenicity screen (EpiScreen) + cynomolgus intravitreal toxicology
safety.note: ESBATech's 2008 PBMC screen flagged two brolucizumab peptides as potentially immunogenic; GMP-lot monkey toxicology showed no ocular effects at 6 mg/eye.
safety.quote: Two sequences (one 8 amino acids, the other 10 amino acids) from the amino acid sequence of brolucizumab were identified as potentially immunogenic, using a screening assay with human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) in vitro
safety.judgement: Year is the ESB01 report date (26 August 2008) as given in the 2019 FDA review, which is the source. The safety model the whole class relies on for DME is cynomolgus intravitreal toxicology (ranibizumab, aflibercept, faricimab, brolucizumab); its first use for the class predates 2008 (ranibizumab) but was not verified within budget. Beovu EPAR (EMA/23630/2020) concluded from the same assays that 'brolucizumab was weakly immunogenic'.

safety.model: In-vitro human PBMC T-cell immunogenicity screen (EpiScreen)
safety.note: FDA reviewer: the in-vitro immunogenicity assays 'correctly predicted ocular inflammation in patients' (HAWK/HARRIER, nAMD); KESTREL/KITE later showed IOI 4.2% vs 1.1% in DME.
safety.short: Assay predicted intraocular inflammation; FDA agreed
safety.quote: This reviewer agrees that clinical data supersede these data, but does not agree that the concern raised is low (i.e. these experiments appear have correctly predicted ocular inflammation in patients).
safety.judgement: Judgement call. The stated comparison (FDA P/T reviewer A. McDougal, BLA 761125) is with nAMD patients (HAWK NCT02307682 / HARRIER NCT02434328) and was published in 2019, before any DME data; DME patients then reproduced the signal (Wykoff 2023, doi:10.1016/j.ajo.2023.07.012: IOI 4.2% vs 1.1% brolucizumab 6 mg vs aflibercept, retinal vasculitis 0.5% vs 0% in KESTREL; KESTREL NCT03481634 results posted 2022-10-28, KITE NCT03481660 posted 2024-01-05). The monkey toxicology the class actually relies on was silent on the GMP lot (NOAEL 6 mg/eye, 'no treatment-related ocular effects') and its pre-GMP inflammation was attributed to endotoxin, so the 'best model' matched only through the in-vitro screen, and occlusive retinal vasculitis specifically was predicted by nothing; neither FDA nor EMA calls the monkey silence a miss, so no contra under rule 1. Abicipar: CEDAR/SEQUOIA (NCT02462928/NCT02462486, results posted 2020-07-28/30) intraocular inflammation was traced to host-cell impurities and fell to 8.9% after a manufacturing change (Callanan 2023 MAPLE, doi:10.2147/OPTH.S405994); its DME phase 2 PALM (NCT02186119) has no posted results and no PubMed paper, so the DME arm of that story is unpublished and no model prediction was ever stated for it. Downgrade this cell to untested if the house rule requires the patient side to be DME.
